correctness.rationale: Reconstructed unrestricted edge-weight optimization for all t≥2, s_i≥1, c_i>0, d_i>0 when s_i≥2, and B>0. Kirchhoff index is strictly convex in the Laplacian on connected designs; distinct edge weights give distinct Laplacians, so the unique minimizer is petal-permutation invariant. Grounding the hub gives M_i=(a_i+s_i b_i)I−b_i J with inverse diagonalized on constants and differences, yielding Kf=Σ[(N−s_i)/a_i+N(s_i−1)/(a_i+s_i b_i)]. The substitution x_i=a_i, y_i=a_i+s_i b_i≥x_i reduces the problem to separate convex C_i/x_i+A_i/y_i terms with budget α_i x_i+β_i y_i. The interior KKT feasibility condition A_iα_i>C_iβ_i is exactly (N−1)d_i<2Nc_i; at equality/upward the one-sided derivative is nonnegative, including cases α_i≤0. Normalizing λ gives all displayed a_i,b_i and minimum S²/B. Independent tests verified 48 threshold regimes, direct grounded resistance comparisons and 28+12√5 bow-tie example; finite checks supplement the analytic all-parameter proof.
residual_risks: Only connectivity-preserving nonnegative allocations; additional lower bounds, nonlinear costs or arbitrary non-clique petals are excluded.
Numerical examples are not proofs of arbitrary real positive edge costs; proof requires strict convexity and complete KKT cases.

value.rationale: Hub-connected cliques model naturally modular resistance networks, and minimization of global Kirchhoff index is a recognized graph-design problem. The sharp N-only ratio controlling exactly when an entire internal edge class should be removed, with a full heterogeneous mixed-regime optimizer, supplies a usable structural sparsification theorem beyond a routine KKT restatement. The size-independent phase frontier is a non-obvious exact invariant; arbitrary costs and petal sizes are included.
residual_risks: The practical interpretation is an ideal linear-cost unconstrained conductance design, not all feasible electrical network deployments.

limitations: One-vertex union of clique petals, fixed positive class costs per edge, linear budget, Kirchhoff index objective only.
